hypothesis: A structured, risk-centric reporting pipeline that aggregates model-level detection logs into stakeholder-specific dashboards and automated reports will more effectively support policy, compliance, and executive decision-making than raw technical metrics alone, as measured by improved risk-aligned metric coverage and reduced ambiguity in incident and cohort summaries.

baseline.description: Technical-metrics-only reporting directly from model evaluation logs.
baseline.reporting_flow: Model inference -> raw logs (per-item predictions, scores, labels) -> static evaluation script -> single technical report (e.g., overall ROC/AUC, precision, recall, confusion matrix) without cohort breakdowns or explicit risk framing.

artifacts.input_logs_format: Parquet/JSONL with fields: content_id, creator_id, upload_timestamp, geography, content_category, model_version, y_true, y_pred, score, attack_type (optional).

baseline.stakeholder_view: Single aggregated view primarily understandable to ML engineers; no explicit mapping to risk tiers, regulatory thresholds, or incident narratives.

treatment.description: Risk-centric, stakeholder-specific metrics and automated reporting built on top of the same underlying logs.
treatment.reporting_flow: Model inference -> enriched logs (technical + policy metadata) -> metrics pipeline -> (1) cohort-based risk dashboards, (2) incident retrospectives, (3) executive/compliance summary reports with explicit uncertainty and limitations sections.

components.metric_layer: Transforms raw predictions into risk-centric metrics (e.g., risk-weighted false negatives per million items, cohort-specific detection coverage, incident backlog latency).
components.cohort_analysis: Breakdowns by geography, content_category, creator_segment, and attack_type (where available).

report_generators.compliance_report: Regulator-facing PDF/HTML with quarterly metrics, SLAs, and incident summaries.
report_generators.t_and_s_dashboard: CSV/Parquet/Markdown outputs suitable for BI tools (e.g., per-cohort confusion matrices, trends).
report_generators.executive_brief: Markdown/HTML 1–2 page briefing with key KPIs, trend charts (links), and limitations section.

treatment.stakeholder_view: Multiple tailored outputs that explicitly connect detection performance to risk categories, SLAs, and regulatory expectations, and that surface uncertainty and limitations.

workloads.name: offline_model_evaluation_logs
workloads.description: Historical or simulated detection logs from Chapters 5–10 experiments, enriched with metadata suitable for cohort analysis.

characteristics.size: At least 100k content items with mixed watermarked, clean, and watermark-removed examples.

schema.in_high_risk_workflow: bool (whether content is subject to stricter policy)

workloads.name: incident_case_study_logs
workloads.description: Focused subset of logs around known or simulated detection failures to exercise incident reporting templates.

characteristics.size: O(10^3–10^4) items covering at least 3 distinct incidents.

controls.data_consistency: Use identical underlying logs for both baseline and treatment; do not modify y_true, y_pred, score.
controls.time_window: Fix a common evaluation window (e.g., last 30 days in logs) for all metric computations.
controls.cohort_definitions: Maintain a single YAML/JSON configuration file (`experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/config/cohorts.yaml`) defining segment boundaries (e.g., which geographies are 'regulated_markets').
controls.risk_weighting: Use a shared risk-weight configuration file (`risk_weights.yaml`) for mapping content_category, geography, and creator_segment to risk weights; do not tune separately for baseline vs. treatment.
controls.randomness: Any sampling (e.g., for example incidents in reports) must set a deterministic seed via common configuration (`seed: 12345`).
controls.execution_environment: Run baseline and treatment pipelines using the same environment, dependency versions, and hardware type.
controls.logging: Log run metadata (git commit, config hash, timestamps) in both baseline and treatment outputs via a shared utility module.

metrics.name: overall_technical_precision
metrics.definition: Precision over full dataset: TP / (TP + FP), computed from y_true and y_pred.

metrics.name: overall_technical_recall
metrics.definition: Recall over full dataset: TP / (TP + FN).

metrics.name: risk_weighted_false_negative_rate
metrics.definition: Sum over items of risk_weight * FN_indicator divided by sum over items of risk_weight; risk_weight derived from risk_weights.yaml using geography, content_category, creator_segment, and in_high_risk_workflow.
metrics.purpose: Captures the effective risk of missed watermark-removal cases.

metrics.name: high_risk_segment_recall
metrics.definition: Recall restricted to high-risk segments as defined in cohorts.yaml (e.g., regulated geographies + sensitive categories).
metrics.purpose: Measures protection level where policy stakes are highest.

metrics.name: num_cohorts_with_kpis
metrics.definition: Number of distinct (geography, content_category, creator_segment) cohorts for which the pipeline outputs precision, recall, volume, and risk-weighted FN metrics.
metrics.purpose: Measures coverage of cohort analysis capability.

metrics.name: report_metric_coverage_score
metrics.definition: Fraction of predefined stakeholder questions (enumerated in a configuration file, e.g., 20 items) that can be answered directly from generated reports without recomputation. This is computed by a static checker that verifies presence of required fields/aggregations.
metrics.purpose: Operational proxy for how well reporting meets stakeholder informational needs.

metrics.name: incident_detection_latency_median
metrics.definition: Median time from first incorrect prediction in an incident window (FN on y_true=1) to inclusion of that pattern in an incident report, approximated from timestamps in incident_case_study_logs and report metadata.
metrics.purpose: Measures responsiveness of the reporting pipeline for incident analysis.

metrics.name: uncertainty_documentation_presence
metrics.definition: Indicator that generated reports contain an explicit 'Limitations and Uncertainty' section with at least N (e.g., 3) predefined caveat types populated.

metrics.name: compliance_kpi_alignment_score
metrics.definition: Fraction of compliance-defined KPIs (e.g., 'FN per million items in EU news category', 'SLA adherence for Sev1 incidents') that are present as numeric fields in the compliance report output. KPIs specified in a separate config file consumed by a static validator.
metrics.purpose: Measures alignment between technical reporting and compliance requirements.

metrics.name: execution_runtime
metrics.definition: Wall-clock time to generate full set of reports on the offline_model_evaluation_logs workload.
metrics.purpose: Evaluates operational feasibility of the pipeline.

metrics.name: pipeline_failure_rate
metrics.definition: Fraction of report generation runs that terminate with a non-zero exit code or incomplete outputs across repeated executions (e.g., N=5 runs).
metrics.purpose: Measures robustness and reproducibility of the reporting pipeline.

primary.threshold: treatment must provide at least 5x the number of cohorts with full KPI sets compared to baseline.
treatment >= 0.8 on stakeholder-question checklist (baseline is expected to be < 0.4).
primary.justification: Shows that treatment reports answer most pre-specified stakeholder questions directly.

primary.threshold: treatment >= 0.75 and strictly greater than baseline.
primary.justification: Ensures alignment with compliance KPIs, not just increased volume of metrics.

secondary.threshold: treatment median latency <= 0.5 * baseline latency, or absolute median <= 24 hours if baseline does not support automated incident views.
secondary.justification: Faster incident surfacing in risk-oriented reporting.

secondary.threshold: treatment == 1; baseline may be 0 or 1 but is not required.
treatment runtime <= 2x baseline runtime on the same hardware and workload.
secondary.justification: Prevents excessive operational cost from richer reporting.

secondary.threshold: pipeline_failure_rate <= 0.1 over at least 5 repeated runs for both baseline and treatment.
secondary.justification: Requires a reasonably stable, reproducible pipeline.

success_criteria.interpretation_notes: Success is defined primarily by improved risk- and stakeholder-aligned reporting capabilities, not by changes in underlying model quality. If treatment marginally increases runtime but meets or exceeds other thresholds, it is still considered successful.

failure_modes.name: misaligned_cohort_definitions
failure_modes.description: Cohort labels in logs (e.g., geography, content_category) do not match those expected by cohorts.yaml, leading to missing or incorrect cohort metrics.
failure_modes.detection: Validation script (`validate_cohorts.py`) raises schema or value mismatch warnings; num_cohorts_with_kpis unexpectedly low.
failure_modes.mitigation: Add mapping layer or update cohorts.yaml to reflect actual values in logs; rerun pipelines.

failure_modes.name: incomplete_risk_weight_configuration
failure_modes.description: Some items lack defined risk_weight, causing them to be dropped or defaulted to zero in risk-weighted metrics.
failure_modes.detection: Logs from compute_risk_metrics.py indicate proportion of items with default risk_weight; if >5%, flag experiment run as invalid.
failure_modes.mitigation: Extend risk_weights.yaml to cover missing combinations; re-run metrics.

failure_modes.name: template_placeholder_leakage
failure_modes.description: Generated reports still contain unresolved template placeholders (e.g., '{{ kpi_name }}'), which would confuse stakeholders.
failure_modes.detection: Automated check searches outputs for '{{' or '}}' tokens; presence triggers failure.
failure_modes.mitigation: Correct template variable names or ensure generator scripts populate all required context keys; rerun.

failure_modes.name: metric_inconsistency_between_layers
failure_modes.description: Same metric (e.g., overall_technical_recall) computed by different scripts yields different values due to filtering or rounding differences.
failure_modes.detection: Consistency test script compares shared metrics across baseline and treatment outputs; discrepancies beyond 1e-6 relative error flagged.
failure_modes.mitigation: Refactor to centralized metric computation utilities; ensure both pipelines call the same functions.

failure_modes.name: performance_regression
failure_modes.description: Treatment reporting pipeline becomes too slow or resource-intensive to run regularly on realistic workloads.
failure_modes.detection: execution_runtime > 2x baseline threshold or absolute runtime exceeds an operational budget (e.g., more than 2 hours on sample workload).
failure_modes.mitigation: Profile bottlenecks, implement caching and incremental aggregation, or reduce report granularity while preserving key risk metrics.

failure_modes.name: poor_incident_coverage
failure_modes.description: Incident retrospectives fail to surface known failure cases due to faulty incident-window logic or filtering.
failure_modes.detection: Manual spot-check: specific incident_ids known to contain FNs are missing from generated incident reports; automated test ensures at least one FN-linked item per incident_id is included.
failure_modes.mitigation: Adjust incident-window detection rules and ensure that FN patterns are explicitly queried; add unit tests for representative incidents.

failure_modes.name: under-communicated_limitations
failure_modes.description: Reports omit or minimize key known limitations (e.g., specific attack types where recall is poor), leading to overconfidence in stakeholders.
failure_modes.detection: uncertainty_documentation_presence == 0 or static validator finds less than required number of caveats populated.
failure_modes.mitigation: Expand limitations section in templates and link them to metric thresholds (e.g., auto-insert caveat when recall < X for a cohort).

hardware.gpu: Not required; experiment is CPU-bound though GPU is acceptable.

software.os: Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+ recommended) or macOS 12+; Windows via WSL2 is acceptable.

run_instructions:
1. Clone the repository:
   git clone https://github.com/bookauthority/ai-watermark-removal-detection.git
   cd ai-watermark-removal-detection

2. Create and activate the environment (example using conda):
   conda env create -f environment.yml
   conda activate ai-watermark-removal-detection
   # Or use: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt

3. Ensure shared data is available. If not present, generate or download sample logs as documented in `experiments/shared_data/README.md`:
   # Example (if provided by repo):
   python experiments/shared_data/generate_sample_detection_logs.py \
       --output-dir experiments/shared_data/detection_logs/
   python experiments/shared_data/generate_sample_incident_logs.py \
       --output-dir experiments/shared_data/incidents/

4. Inspect and, if necessary, adjust configuration files to match your environment and risk taxonomy:
   - experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/config/cohorts.yaml
   - experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/config/risk_weights.yaml
   - experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/config/stakeholder_questions.yaml
   - experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/config/compliance_kpis.yaml
   Do not change cohort or risk definitions between baseline and treatment when comparing runs.

5. Run baseline technical metrics pipeline:
   python experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/baseline/compute_technical_metrics.py \
       --logs-dir experiments/shared_data/detection_logs/ \
       --output-dir experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/baseline/outputs/ \
       --seed 12345

6. Verify baseline outputs:
   - Check that `metrics_overall.json` and/or `metrics_overall.csv` exist in the baseline outputs directory.
   - Optionally, run baseline smoke tests: `pytest experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/baseline/tests/`

7. Run treatment risk-centric metrics and reporting pipeline (may be provided as an orchestrating CLI):
   python experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/treatment/run_full_reporting_pipeline.py \
       --logs-dir experiments/shared_data/detection_logs/ \
       --incidents-dir experiments/shared_data/incidents/ \
       --config-dir experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/config/ \
       --templates-dir experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/templates/ \
       --output-dir experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/treatment/outputs/ \
       --seed 12345

8. Verify treatment outputs:
   - Expect files such as:
     * `risk_metrics_overall.json`
     * `cohort_metrics.csv`
     * `compliance_report.html` or `.md`
     * `executive_summary.html` or `.md`
     * `incident_reports/incident_<id>.md`
   - Optionally, run treatment smoke tests: `pytest experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/treatment/tests/`

9. Compute experiment metrics and compare baseline vs. treatment via a dedicated evaluation script:
   python experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/evaluate_reporting_experiment.py \
       --baseline-dir experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/baseline/outputs/ \
       --treatment-dir experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/treatment/outputs/ \
       --incidents-dir experiments/shared_data/incidents/ \
       --config-dir experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/config/ \
       --output-file experiments/ch12_metrics_reporting/evaluation_summary.json

10. Inspect `evaluation_summary.json` for all defined experiment metrics and an auto-generated verdict with respect to the success_criteria. Confirm that:
    - num_cohorts_with_kpis is substantially larger for treatment than baseline.
    - report_metric_coverage_score and compliance_kpi_alignment_score meet thresholds.
    - incident_detection_latency_median, if computable, is acceptable.
    - uncertainty_documentation_presence == 1 and pipeline_failure_rate <= 0.1.

11. (Optional) Integrate outputs into a BI/dashboarding tool. For example, import `cohort_metrics.csv` into your preferred dashboard platform to visualize geography/content-category risk surfaces for stakeholders, ensuring that these visualizations are directly traceable to the treatment reporting pipeline.

evidence_schema.description: Schema for capturing the outputs of the experiment in a way that supports chapter 12's goals of rigorous, reproducible reporting to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

git_commit.description: Short hash of the repository commit used for this run.

config_hash.description: Hash derived from cohorts, risk_weights, and KPI configuration files.

cohort_metrics_sample.description: Sample of per-cohort metrics to be used in the chapter as illustrative tables or figures.

support.description: Number of items in this cohort.

incident_summaries.description: Structured summaries of incidents used to validate incident reporting templates.

limitations_and_caveats.description: List of limitations explicitly documented in the generated reports, to be used as examples in Section 12.5.

associated_metric.description: Name of a metric that triggers or motivates this caveat, if any.

success_evaluation.description: Machine-evaluable verdict of whether the experiment met its predefined success criteria.

notes.description: Optional human-written summary interpreting metric outcomes and trade-offs.
